headline: Math is nearly solved; agents doing real work remain the frontier
outlook: Math is the clearest success story of the past year: the field closed 95% of the remaining headroom on math benchmarks, FrontierMath and FrontierMath Tier 4 both passed 90%, and GPT-6.1 Sol has just posted 100% on Tier 4. Agents and real work are moving much more slowly, with only 32% of headroom closed, the Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, which is why those 90% milestones sit in mid-2027 and 2028 on current fits. Task length is the most direct measure of progress toward real work. Claude Mythos Preview now handles tasks of about 17.4 hours, the horizon has been doubling roughly every 4.2 months, and on current trends a full 40-hour work-week is most likely around December 2026, with a 90% range running to March 2027. Costs keep falling as capability rises: the price of reaching 80% or better on GPQA has dropped from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens, and the trend points below a cent in early 2027. Not everything follows its curve, though; Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are stuck just short of 90% months after their fits said they would cross, a reminder that the last few points can stall and that forecasts built on only a handful of records carry wide ranges.
